newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SBI cuts prime rate to 14.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: India's SBI cuts prime rate to 14.0 pct.

text.p: The State Bank of India (SBI), the country's largest commercial bank, said on Tuesday it decided to lower its prime lending rate to 14.0 percent from 14.5 percent.
The new rate would be effective from April 16, a bank official said on Tuesday. The spread over the prime rate was unchanged at 3.75 percent, he said.

The rate cut follows the 1997/98 (April-March) first half credit policy announcement by the Reserve Bank of India, which cut the maximum deposit interest rate from 10 percent to nine percent to prompt lending rate cuts by banks.
The bank also decided to reduce the interest rate on export credit to 12.5 percent from 13.0 percent per annum earlier, the official said.
RBI also changed its prescription on the interest rate on post-shipment rupee export credit upto 90 days from 13.0 percent per annum to "not exceeding 13.0 percent per annum."
